notes.text: The sheet is a landscape double leaf with handwritten folio 1, a wide left discussion and narrower right continuation. It develops specialization preorders, the associated topology on a preorder, two functors and an adjunction, then asks which preorders a pseudo-partition determines. The upper-right asterisk note asks “quelles conditions supplémentaires ... imposer pour avoir unicité ?”. This is a report of source contents, not verification of its claims.

Several apparent slips are preserved: the NB1 closure equivalence uses a written ≤ where the earlier definition uses subset; the two identity subscripts are written E then O; the Posons insertion appears to use inverse image of I although its left index is J; the summand in the left closure formula is unstarred X_j. These are visual diagnostics only. Parent will append any independently performed mathematical checks.

Source grammar is not regularized. The current text retains cette préordre; the noun/agreement in les réunions ... est fermé is now explicitly doubtful, and singular partition is preferred with partitions as an alternative. The initial capital A before quelles has no written accent. The identity-map explanation still has no closing parenthesis after NB2. No missing word or punctuation has been supplied.

Whole image and both supplied native halves were inspected once; required places P01–P52 were inspected once each. P53 completes only the clipped extreme-right punctuation of P35. P54 inspects previously uncropped specialization underlining. P55 was a clipped context fragment; P56 completes only its missing NB. 2 heading. No OCR, outside research or TeX compilation was used. line_count counts nonempty logical draft lines, including display and diagram rows.

The short horizontal stroke below the adjunction explanation is rendered as a paragraph separator. Its source position starts far left of I→X and lies below the sentence baseline, so it is not assigned as a certain underline.

Targeted check from the definitions on this sheet: x ≤ y iff closure{x} ⊆ closure{y} makes every open upward closed. In the associated preorder topology, closure{x}=I_{≤x}, so its specialization preorder recovers the original one. A map I→X is continuous iff it is monotone: continuity preserves specialization; conversely the inverse image of each X-open is upward closed and therefore open in I. This establishes the stated Hom correspondence under those definitions.

The category labels in the source make Ord∘Esp an endofunctor of O and Esp∘Ord an endofunctor of E. The visually confirmed right-hand identity subscripts are nevertheless E then O. Both are preserved literally; exchanging them is only a typing diagnostic, not an emendation.

Targeted check: closure{i} intersected with the smallest open containing i is the preorder-equivalence class of i. Its equality to {i} for every i is equivalent to antisymmetry. This explains the two opposite decorations in the source; it does not change any written mark.

Targeted check of the local-finiteness claim: if φ has locally finite image, then on a neighborhood of each point only finitely many fibers occur. Restrictions of saturated sets to that neighborhood therefore have only finitely many possible forms. An arbitrary union of saturated closed sets restricts to a finite union of closed restrictions, so is closed locally, hence globally. Thus arbitrary unions of quotient-closed sets are quotient-closed. The source singular agreement and its use of ordre versus préordre remain untouched.

Blind-audit findings: distinguish the unaccented baseline ordonne and left definition label def from separately accented occurrences. The terminal NB1 mark is a dash. The finite-case explanation has a closing parenthesis but no secure opening one. Final finie in the explanation of local finiteness is written with a small e. New uncertainties that preserve the preferred C reading are recorded as doubts, not new primary corrections.

Audit scope limitation: neutral box B18 contains the already-transcribed I→X but misses the paragraph rule. The main reader inspected saved original crop P17, which includes both. The separator is retained on that independent visual evidence; the fixed second reading has not been altered or represented as having read the missing rule.

The lower indexing clause is raised and independently underlined above a separate heavy cancellation. The low group beneath it favors qui filtre, with tels que retained as an alternative. The nearby telle que after disjoints et follows the rising baseline in the wider image; it is not asserted to be a separate insertion.
